fixes.explanation: That's the one, baker. The text says they set out from Mount Hor along the route to the Red Sea "…in order to bypass the land of Edom." So the passage gives us the reason for the route, and that's your answer. I've taken the long way around my own kitchen to dodge a pan I burned, so I get it.

Elim is a place from earlier in Israel's journey (Exodus 15:27), and it isn't what this verse is about. Here the text says they set out from Mount Hor along the route to the Red Sea, in order to bypass the land of Edom. The detour was about getting around Edom. I've picked the wrong oven setting plenty of times myself, so no worries.

Jethro is the priest of Midian and Moses' father-in-law (Exodus 3:1). He's a real name from Moses' story, but he isn't in this passage. The text says they were going the long way "…in order to bypass the land of Edom." That's the whole reason given. Good guess for a name that sounds like it belongs, friend.

Yes, baker. The text says the people "…grew impatient on the journey". Their patience ran out somewhere along the way. I know that feeling. I once got antsy waiting for a batch to cool, and that's a ten minute wait.

That's right. The people "…spoke against God and against Moses…" and Moses is Israel's leader. So the complaint went to God and to the man leading them. I think that's a tough spot to stand in, and I bet Moses felt it.

Aaron is Moses' brother (Exodus 4:14), but this verse doesn't mention him. The text says the people "…spoke against God and against Moses…" The blank is Moses. It's an easy name to grab, friend, since Aaron is a name you meet around Moses.

Joshua was Moses' attendant (Exodus 24:13), but he isn't named in this verse. Here the people "…spoke against God and against Moses…" So Moses fills the blank. Good try, friend. Joshua's a name worth knowing, but he's not in this complaint.

Egypt does come up in their complaint, when they say "Why have you led us up out of Egypt to die in the wilderness?" (Numbers 21:5). But the request they bring to Moses is different: "Intercede with the LORD so He will take the snakes away from us." The ask is about the snakes, friend.

Yes, baker. The LORD tells Moses, "Make a fiery serpent and mount it on a pole." Picture Moses hearing that one. I bet he had questions, and I'd have had a whole list. But the text says he did it: he made a bronze snake and mounted it on a pole (Numbers 21:9).

A golden lampstand is a real item in the Bible (Exodus 25:31), but it isn't what the LORD asks for here. He says, "Make a fiery serpent and mount it on a pole." The pole is the clue, friend. A lampstand would've been a lot less scary to carve.
People do bow in the Bible, like in Exodus 4:31, but bowing isn't the word here. The LORD says, "When anyone who is bitten looks at it, he will live." The word is looks, friend. No bowing needed.
